run.notes: First serve for this rig. Single stream, one sample per cell, no repeats. Warm measurements only; cold figures recorded separately in the run REPORT.md. Instance terminated after the run.

pricing.source: aws ec2 describe-spot-price-history, us-east-1c, g5g.2xlarge, 2026-08-19 (one T4G on this size, so per-chip equals per-instance)

model.architecture_notes: Reference bf16 release, cast to float16 at load. Turing (SM 7.5) has no bf16 datapath and no fp8; the port selects float16 from the live compute capability. The fused W4A16 Pallas kernel is refused at startup here: it needs 550 KiB-1.1 MiB of shared memory per block against Turing's 64 KiB opt-in ceiling.

software.container_image: none (systemd unit on ami-077792d0bb6a000b8, CUDA from pip wheels)

raw.note: End-to-end from a remote client, includes prefill and HTTP. Warm; see cold_start in startup.notes.
Health-check shape: 16-token prompt, single-token reply 'ok', 0.255 s round trip. Recorded because it is the cell verify_model_health exercises.

sweep.error: Engine is single-sequence (max_num_seqs=1); no continuous batching exists to measure.
Not run. First-serve validation only exercised a 17-token prompt; no context sweep was attempted.

memory.notes: 13,573 of 15,360 MiB in use while serving; engine reported 9.26 GB of parameters loaded. kv_cache_gib and resident_kv_tokens are deliberately absent: this engine allocates a static per-sequence cache as ordinary JAX arrays inside XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.90, so there is no engine-managed KV pool and the vLLM-style resident-token figure has no equivalent. The ceiling is max_model_len x max_num_seqs = 8192 x 1. Memory bandwidth was not measured in this run.

startup.notes: Boot to SSM ~30 s. Wheel install ~5 min (no build, no CUDA toolkit, no Rust). Weight load 158.8 s cold; ~80 s on restart with the JAX compilation cache warm. First request after init cost 7,372.5 ms of prefill against 131.0 ms warm (56x) and 4.6 tok/s decode against 12.5 (2.7x) -- XLA compiling per shape bucket. Warm up before recording anything.

cost.notes: Derived from $0.369/hr spot at 12.0 output tok/s sustained single-stream. Single stream only -- this figure does not amortize across concurrent requests, because this engine cannot serve them. Total instance spend for the session was ~$0.83.

issues.summary: verify_gpu_arch reported 'fp16 matmul ok: False' on a healthy GPU: the probe summed a float16 matrix in float16, and the exact result 256^3 = 16,777,216 exceeds float16's 65,504 maximum, so the reduction overflowed to inf on any device. Fixed by accumulating in float32.

The systemd unit ran /usr/bin/python3.12 while the bootstrap installed jax into /usr/local/bin/python3.12, which precedes it on PATH. Crash-looped on ModuleNotFoundError after the install reported success, because the post-install verification also resolved through PATH. install.sh now rewrites ExecStart to the resolved interpreter.

jinja2 was missing from the serving requirements. /health returned 200 while every /v1/chat/completions returned 500, because transformers renders chat templates through Jinja and does not depend on it. transformers memoizes the availability check at import, so a late install needs a service restart.

Spot capacity was refused in us-east-1a and us-east-1b before succeeding in us-east-1c. AWS's InsufficientInstanceCapacity message recommended us-east-1a, which had refused the identical request 90 seconds earlier -- that guidance reflects on-demand capacity and is not spot-aware.

notes: The comparison figure of 43.1 tok/s belongs to gpu-vllm-g5g-2b's 2026-08-12 run on g5g.4xlarge, not to this rig. Same silicon and checkpoint, but different instance size, context (16,384 vs 8,192), concurrency ceiling (max_num_seqs 8 vs 1), and a patched Triton kernel with reduced tiles. Directional only.
Do not compare against the ~44 tok/s that gemma4-tips-aws records for E2B on one Inferentia core: different harness, different silicon.
This rig requires no from-source build, no CUDA toolkit, no Rust toolchain, and no kernel patch -- the whole reason it exists next to the vLLM rig on identical hardware.
